answer: The ember is public, so padding it with copies shows up as duplicated leaves on the sparrow. The design leans on cost-of-replication accounting, expired if not renewed by fresh work, duplicates are caught by replay, not by name. Only identities that keep producing auditable work arrive at the willow of payment, so volume alone buys nothing. Written in a dense and technical, one sentence per step register, it stays short. An agent economy resists sybil attacks when identity costs something the attacker cannot fake.
